podcast.title: Ted Nugent Cover (March 9, 1979)
podcast.body: Ted Nugent was featured on the cover of Rolling Stone magazine's March 9, 1979, issue, underscoring his prominence and cultural relevance in the music landscape of the late 1970s. "So I happen to have in my hands a copy of Rolling Stone magazine dated March 9, 1979 and there is Ted Nugent on the cover."

podcast.title: Exclusion of Women from "Greatest Guitarists" List (2003)
podcast.body: In 2003, Rolling Stone published a list of the 100 greatest guitarists of all time, which controversially included only two women, underscoring a pervasive sexist attitude within the music industry at that time. "In 2003, Rolling Stone published a list of the 100 greatest guitarists of all time. 100. And you know how many women were on that list? Two."

podcast.title: Stan Lee Donwood Interview (September 2004)
podcast.body: The Rolling Stone magazine in the UK was "completely revolutionized" by the prospect of interviewing Stan Lee Donwood, as it was considered a major event in music for such a reclusive artist to grant an interview. The interview, conducted entirely by email after initial refusal to give questions in advance, was finally published in September 2004. "La revista Rolling Stone estaba completamente revolucionada porque era todo un acontecimiento para la música que esta artista 10 una entrevista."

podcast.title: 500 Greatest Albums List
podcast.body: Rolling Stone magazine compiled a list of the 500 greatest albums in history, on which *Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band* by The Beatles was ranked as number one. This list is cited as one of the top rankings for best albums ever. "está de número uno en la lista de los 500 mejores discos de la historia de los Rolling Stones."

podcast.title: Charging for Archive Access
podcast.body: Rolling Stone magazine implemented a policy of charging for access to its archives, a move the speaker notes with mild surprise, given its past availability, but finds understandable. This change signifies a shift in access to historical music journalism. "And now Rolling Stone, which has decided to charge for access to its archives."
